To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed folded slice-wise approach is the best choice in terms of efficiency and performance.
the folding of the SHA-2 hash functions is a promising approach for the SHA-3 implementations on FPGAs.

the SHA-3 Keccak algorithm can be efficiently implemented in FPGAs, that the folding technique is the key for efficient FPGA implementations of the SHA3 algorithm and that the folding can be performed slice-wise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the FPGA-based hardware implementation of the Keccak SHA-3 hash function.
the efficient implementation of the SHA-2 and SHA-3 hash function.
the following questions: What is the best FPGA implementation strategy to achieve high performance for the SHA-3 hashing function?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best solution is to implement the SHA-3 Keccak algorithm in the folded slice-wise manner.
the folded structure is the most efficient solution for FPGA based SHA-3 implementations, and that this is the case for both, area and performance.
the folded slice-wise structures are the most efficient structures in terms of area, while pipelined and unfolded structures are the best choice in regard to the throughput.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed slice-wise folding technique allows to achieve the best efficiency in terms of throughput per area.
it is possible to achieve an efficiency of 0.5 gbps per slice, which means that a single Virtex-5 LX110T FPGA can provide 1 Gbps of throughput.
the proposed folded structures are more efficient than the existing state of art and the proposed pipelined structure achieves the best performance in terms of frequency and throughput.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the folding/unrolling options can be used to achieve a significant improvement in terms of efficiency.
the folding of the datapath can be used to achieve a significant improvement in the efficiency of the SHA-2 and SHA-3 FPGA implementations.
it is possible to achieve a better performance-cost tradeoff than the current state of the art for the SHA-3 Keccak hashing functions.
